statements.status_notes: Spring Framework MVC applications can be vulnerable to a "Path Traversal Vulnerability" when deployed on a non-compliant Servlet container. An application can be vulnerable when all the following are true: the application is deployed as a WAR or with an embedded Servlet container; the Servlet container does not reject suspicious sequences; the application serves static resources with Spring resource handling. Applications deployed on Apache Tomcat or Eclipse Jetty are not vulnerable, as long as default security features are not disabled in the configuration.
statements.impact_statement: The Liquibase CLI contains no Spring code. The scanner reports spring-webmvc from the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz). It runs only if a user extracts and starts it. The application carries spring-webmvc 6.2.2 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, which is in range; 5.0.3 and later carry 6.2.12 or 7.0.x, which are not affected. The advisory needs a Servlet container that does not reject suspicious path sequences; Spring verified that applications on Apache Tomcat are not vulnerable unless its default security features are disabled. The application runs on embedded Tomcat with default settings: it sets no server properties and none of its classes references the Tomcat API. The advisory also needs static resources served through Spring resource handling. The application registers no resource handlers of its own; Spring Boot's default handler maps only the classpath locations static, public, resources and META-INF/resources, and neither the application nor any of its bundled libraries packages content there.

statements.status_notes: Spring MVC and WebFlux applications are vulnerable to stream corruption when using Server-Sent Events (SSE). This issue affects Spring Framework: from 7.0.0 through 7.0.5, from 6.2.0 through 6.2.16, from 6.1.0 through 6.1.25, from 5.3.0 through 5.3.46.
statements.impact_statement: The Liquibase CLI contains no Spring code. The scanner reports spring-webmvc from the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz). The application carries spring-webmvc 6.2.2 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, 6.2.12 in 5.0.3 and 7.0.3 in 5.1.0, all in range, and the fixed 7.0.6 in 5.1.1 and later. The stream corruption occurs only in an application that streams Server-Sent Events. A source review of the application found no SseEmitter, ServerSentEvent, text/event-stream or WebFlux usage: its controllers are @RestController classes returning plain JSON, text or hand-rendered HTML bodies, so the SSE writing path is never executed.

This issue affects Spring Framework: from 7.0.0 through 7.0.5, from 6.2.0 through 6.2.16, from 6.1.0 through 6.1.25, from 5.3.0 through 5.3.46.
statements.impact_statement: The Liquibase CLI contains no Spring code. The application carries spring-webmvc 6.2.2 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, 6.2.12 in 5.0.3 and 7.0.3 in 5.1.0, all in range, and the fixed 7.0.6 in 5.1.1 and later. The advisory requires an application that renders script template views (ScriptTemplateView) through a Java scripting engine such as JRuby or Jython. statements.status_notes: Spring MVC and WebFlux applications are vulnerable to cache poisoning when resolving static resources. More precisely, an application can be vulnerable when all the following are true: the application is using Spring MVC or Spring WebFlux; the application is configuring the resource chain support with caching enabled; the application adds support for encoded resources resolution; the resource cache must be empty when the attacker has access to the application. When all the conditions above are met, the attacker can send malicious requests and poison the resource cache with resources using the wrong encoding. This can cause a denial of service by breaking the front-end application for clients.
statements.impact_statement: The Liquibase CLI contains no Spring code. The scanner reports spring-webmvc from the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz). It runs only if a user extracts and starts it. The application carries spring-webmvc 6.2.2 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, 6.2.12 in 5.0.3, 7.0.3 in 5.1.0 and 7.0.6 in 5.1.1, all in range; 5.2.0 and later carry 7.0.7 or newer, which include the fix. The advisory needs the application to configure the Spring resource chain with caching enabled and to add encoded resource resolution. The application packages no static resources, sets no spring.web.resources properties, and none of its own classes registers a resource handler or resource resolver. Spring Boot's default resource handlers run without the resource chain and its cache, which Boot enables only when the resource-chain properties are set. Its only controllers are three @RestController classes with explicit v1/track, v1/report and v1/health paths.

statements.status_notes: Spring MVC and WebFlux applications are vulnerable to Denial of Service attacks when resolving static resources. More precisely, an application can be vulnerable when all the following are true: the application is using Spring MVC or Spring WebFlux; the application is serving static resources from the file system; the application is running on a Windows platform. When all the conditions above are met, the attacker can send malicious requests that are slow to resolve and that can keep HTTP connections in use. This can cause a Denial of Service on the application.

The advisory needs the application to serve static resources from the file system and to run on Windows. The application packages no static resources, sets no spring.web.resources properties, and none of its own classes registers a resource handler, so it serves nothing from the file system; Spring Boot's default static locations are classpath locations only. statements.status_notes: Spring MVC and WebFlux applications are vulnerable to Denial of Service (DoS) attacks when resolving static resources. An application can be vulnerable when it uses Spring MVC or Spring WebFlux, serves static resources from the file system, and has configured versioned resources support. Affected versions: Spring Framework 7.0.0 through 7.0.7; 6.2.0 through 6.2.18; 6.1.0 through 6.1.27; 5.3.48 and earlier.
statements.impact_statement: The Liquibase CLI contains no Spring code. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz). The application carries spring-webmvc 6.2.2 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, 6.2.12 in 5.0.3, 7.0.3 in 5.1.0, 7.0.6 in 5.1.1 and 7.0.7 in 5.2.0, all in range, and the fixed 7.0.8 in 5.2.1 and 5.2.2. The advisory requires an application that serves static resources from the file system and has versioned resource support configured. The application configures neither: it packages no static resources, sets no spring.web.resources static-location or resource-chain properties, and none of its own classes references VersionResourceResolver, ResourceChainRegistration or a resource-handler registry. Spring Boot registers versioned resource resolution only when the resource-chain strategy properties are set.

statements.status_notes: A Spring MVC or Spring WebFlux application which configures a mapping for "/**" where the view name is not explicitly specified allows an attacker to craft a link resulting in a 302 redirect to an arbitrary external host via the redirect: prefix. Affected versions: Spring Framework 7.0.0 through 7.0.7; 6.2.0 through 6.2.18; 6.1.0 through 6.1.27; 5.3.48 and earlier.
statements.impact_statement: The Liquibase CLI contains no Spring code. The application carries spring-webmvc 6.2.2 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, 6.2.12 in 5.0.3, 7.0.3 in 5.1.0, 7.0.6 in 5.1.1 and 7.0.7 in 5.2.0, all in range, and the fixed 7.0.8 in 5.2.1 and 5.2.2. The advisory requires a "/**" mapping that resolves to view rendering without an explicit view name, so that the view name is derived from the request path and a "redirect:" prefix can be injected. A source and bytecode review of the application found no view controllers, ViewResolver, ModelAndView, WebMvcConfigurer or "/**" handler mapping of its own. Its only controllers are three @RestController classes with explicit v1/track, v1/report and v1/health paths that return response bodies, never view names.

statements.status_notes: Due to incorrect escaping, the use of JavaScriptUtils.javaScriptEscape() may lead to JavaScript code injection in the browser, potentially resulting in a cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability. Affected versions: Spring Framework 7.0.0 through 7.0.7; 6.2.0 through 6.2.18; 6.1.0 through 6.1.27; 5.3.48 and earlier.
statements.impact_statement: The Liquibase CLI contains no Spring code. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz). The application carries spring-webmvc 6.2.2 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, 6.2.12 in 5.0.3, 7.0.3 in 5.1.0, 7.0.6 in 5.1.1 and 7.0.7 in 5.2.0, all in range, and the fixed 7.0.8 in 5.2.1 and 5.2.2. A bytecode scan of the application found JavaScriptUtils called only from the Spring JSP tag classes (EscapeBodyTag, EvalTag, MessageTag and UrlTag). The application bundles no JSP engine and renders no JSP views, and none of its own classes calls JavaScriptUtils.javaScriptEscape(), so the faulty escaping never runs.

statements.status_notes: Spring MVC applications which accept user-supplied values in the cssClass, cssErrorClass, or cssStyle attributes of JSP form tags allow arbitrary HTML/JavaScript code injection, potentially resulting in a cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability. Affected versions: Spring Framework 7.0.0 through 7.0.7; 6.2.0 through 6.2.18; 6.1.0 through 6.1.27; 5.3.48 and earlier.
statements.impact_statement: The Liquibase CLI contains no Spring code. The scanner reports spring-webmvc from the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz). It runs only if a user extracts and starts it. The application carries spring-webmvc 6.2.2 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, 6.2.12 in 5.0.3, 7.0.3 in 5.1.0, 7.0.6 in 5.1.1 and 7.0.7 in 5.2.0, all in range, and the fixed 7.0.8 in 5.2.1 and 5.2.2. The flaw is in the Spring JSP form tag library, which runs only when JSP pages are rendered. The application contains no JSP files or taglib declarations and does not bundle a JSP engine (tomcat-embed-jasper), so Spring form tags are never executed. Its one HTML report is rendered with mustache.java from a fixed template, not through Spring views.

statements.status_notes: Spring MVC and WebFlux applications are vulnerable to Multipart request smuggling attacks. Affected versions: Spring Framework 7.0.0 through 7.0.7; 6.2.0 through 6.2.18; 6.1.0 through 6.1.27; 5.3.48 and earlier.
statements.impact_statement: The Liquibase CLI contains no Spring code. The scanner reports spring-webmvc from the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz). It runs only if a user extracts and starts it. The application carries spring-webmvc 6.2.2 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, 6.2.12 in 5.0.3, 7.0.3 in 5.1.0, 7.0.6 in 5.1.1 and 7.0.7 in 5.2.0, all in range, and the fixed 7.0.8 in 5.2.1 and 5.2.2. The advisory needs an application that accepts multipart requests and sits behind a web application firewall or proxy that parses multipart bodies and makes security decisions on their content, so that a request the firewall reads as harmless is parsed differently by Spring. Spring Boot registers its standard multipart resolver by default and the application does not turn it off, but no handler accepts multipart content. Its only controllers are three @RestController classes: v1/track takes a JSON @RequestBody, and v1/report and v1/health are GET methods without parameters. None of its classes references MultipartFile, @RequestPart, @RequestParam, a MultipartResolver or the servlet request, and it sets no spring.servlet.multipart properties. Liquibase ships no firewall or proxy in front of it.

statements.status_notes: Use of XsltView in a Spring MVC application can result in SSRF and RCE attack if the application has an "/**" mapping that results in view rendering, and where the view name is not explicitly specified. Affected versions: Spring Framework 7.0.0 - 7.0.8; 6.2.0 - 6.2.19; 6.1.0 - 6.1.28; 6.0.0 - 6.0.30; 5.3.0 - 5.3.49; 5.2.25.RELEASE and earlier.
statements.impact_statement: The scanner reports spring-webmvc from the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Liquibase Secure Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz); the Liquibase CLI itself contains no Spring MVC code. The application bundles spring-webmvc 6.2.2 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, 6.2.12 in 5.0.3, 7.0.3 in 5.1.0, 7.0.6 in 5.1.1, 7.0.7 in 5.2.0 and 7.0.8 in 5.2.1 and 5.2.2, all in range. The advisory requires an application that renders views through XsltView, has a "/**" mapping that leads to view rendering, and leaves the view name implicit. A source review of the application found no XsltView, XsltViewResolver, ViewResolver or ModelAndView references, no .xsl resources, no spring.mvc.view properties and no "/**" mapping. All three of its controllers are @RestController classes with explicit v1/track, v1/report and v1/health paths that return response bodies, never view names; its one HTML report is rendered by hand with mustache.java, not through a Spring view.
